macro.topic: Strong PMI data and hawkish Fed signals pushed Treasury yields to their post-2007 high

views.view: Wrote that September flash PMI hitting a more-than-five-year high, Fed Governor Barr's signal of a further hike, and a weak 5-year Treasury auction combined to send yields sharply higher, with October hike odds nearing 70%.
views.quote: Fed Governor Barr's signal of a further hike combined with a weak 5-year Treasury auction to send yields sharply higher; October hike odds are nearing 70%.

views.view: Wrote that the 10-year yield climbed to 5.07%, its highest since 2007, coinciding with rising oil prices and inflation risk, and that the discount rate applied to high-multiple tech and AI stocks is shifting materially.
views.quote: With the 10-year above 5%, the discount rate for high-multiple tech and AI stocks is changing materially.

views.view: Assessed that September flash PMI coming in well above expectations pushed Treasury yields higher across all maturities, creating the risk of a choppy, two-sided market that is not a good environment for taking swing positions.
views.quote: We may see a choppy market with sharp two-way moves where direction is hard to find in this period. It helps to be cautious when taking positions and pay attention to risk management.

macro.topic: US-China trade truce extended to January 10

views.view: Shared that Treasury Secretary Bessent said the trade truce under the Busan agreement, originally set to expire in November, was extended two months to January 10 after unplanned talks in Washington, during which a broader economic package could be reached.
views.quote: Secretary Bessent said that during the extended period a more comprehensive economic package could be agreed, or the current terms could again be extended going forward.

views.view: Shared that after Bessent's meeting with Vice Premier He Lifeng the truce was extended to January 10, that a potentially bigger trade deal was also discussed but not confirmed, and that Trump and Xi are expected to meet four times this year.
views.quote: He says they also discussed a potentially bigger trade deal, though 'don't know if [it] can be done.' Trump and Xi are also expected to meet 4 times this year.

views.quote: White House official: reports that the U.S. is considering a diesel export ban are untrue.

persons.name: Ahmet Sunelcan
persons.digest:
Ahmet Sunelcan focused mostly on portfolio management and valuation today: he wrote that he chose to add to **FPS** rather than KLAC, because FPS fell from $50 to $25 and recovered to around $30-31 on strong balance-sheet and backlog numbers, and reminded followers not to be scared by a one-off charge in its next earnings report. He said he finds **AVGO** attractively valued but is wary of its market-cap size. He isn't adding to space stocks (**RKLB**, **ASTS**), seeing them as still expensive on the metrics, has given up entirely on Planet Labs because of its dilution, and closed a small **MRLN** position at a heavy loss.

On energy infrastructure, he said he sees **Vertiv** as higher quality long term while **Modine** could grow faster in the near term. He assessed that September flash PMI beating expectations pushed Treasury yields higher across all maturities, creating the risk of a choppy, two-sided market not suited to swing positions. He also recalled that the unwinding of extremely leveraged positions (4x software shorts paired with 4x hardware longs) in June-July weighed heavily on AI hardware stocks for a month.
